slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications
slides.section: 1.1.1 - Ethical and Legal Issues in Information System

content.title: Ethical and Legal Issues in Information Systems
key_points: Ethics = principles of making right or wrong decisions
Technology creates new situations not covered by traditional laws
• Privacy – unauthorized access to personal data
• Information Gathering – consent for data collection
• Information Security & Liability – protecting data and reporting breaches
In Ethiopia, report cyber breaches to INSA
content.visual_suggestion: Icon grid showing 4 issues (lock, copyright, database, shield)

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications

content.title: Social Issues in Information Systems
key_points: Social Media & Gaming Addiction – impairs life areas
Plagiarism – presenting others' work as your own
Cybercrime – fraud, identity theft, privacy violations
Automation & Job Displacement – routine jobs lost, new skills needed
Students should be mindful, responsible digital citizens
content.visual_suggestion: Split screen – positive vs negative social impacts

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications
slides.section: 1.1.3 - Environmental Issues Caused by Information Systems

content.title: Environmental Issues from Information Systems
key_points: E-waste – discarded electronics with toxic materials
E-waste Management – systematic collection, recycling, safe disposal
Responsibility: use and dispose of tech smartly
content.visual_suggestion: Diagram showing e-waste cycle and green tech icons

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications
slides.section: 1.1.4 - Health Issues Caused by Information Systems

content.title: Health Issues from Information Systems
key_points: Mental health: sleeping disorders, stress, loss of attention
Musculoskeletal problems: back, neck, shoulders, wrists
Solution: take breaks, maintain good posture, use devices responsibly
Balance benefits of health IT with mindful usage
content.visual_suggestion: Body diagram highlighting affected areas

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications

content.title: Intellectual Property Rights
key_points: Intellectual Property = intangible rights over creative works
• Trade Secrets – confidential business info (e.g., Coca-Cola recipe)
• Patents – exclusive rights for inventions (e.g., Google PageRank)
• Copyrights – automatic protection for original works (e.g., software)
• Trademarks – signs distinguishing goods/services (e.g., Microsoft logo)
Ethiopian Intellectual Property Office (EIPO) manages IP applications
content.visual_suggestion: 4 boxes with icons for each IP type

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications

content.title: Digital Identity Management
key_points: Digital Identity = online collection of information about a person
Verification methods: documents, biometrics, database checks
Ethiopia: National ID project under Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy
content.visual_suggestion: Infographic of identity verification methods

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications

content.title: Digital Collaboration
key_points: Digital collaboration = working together using digital tools
• Collaborative Tools – communication, file sharing, project management
Tool examples: Teams, Zoom, Google Drive, Trello, Tableau, OneNote
content.visual_suggestion: Three pillars: People, Tools, Devices

slides.chapter: Unit 1: Information Systems and their Applications
slides.section: 1.5 - Engaging in Citizenship through Digital Technologies

content.title: Digital Citizenship
key_points: Poor citizenship: cyberbullying, careless sharing, ignoring safety
content.visual_suggestion: Image of GERD with social media icons

content.title: Big Data: The 5 V's
key_points: Big Data = massive, complex datasets hard to process traditionally
Applications: healthcare, education, banking, agriculture, retail, transport
Challenges: growth, security, lack of skilled professionals
content.visual_suggestion: 5 V's diagram with icons

content.title: Cloud Computing
key_points: Delivery of computing services over the Internet
Limitations: downtime, security/privacy, data ownership concerns
• PaaS – platform for development (e.g., Windows Azure)
content.visual_suggestion: Cloud diagram with service models and types

content.title: Fog Computing
key_points: Extension of cloud computing – processes data closer to source
Fog nodes near data sources have higher processing power
Benefits: low latency, location awareness, reduced bandwidth use
Processes data locally then sends summary to cloud
Essential for real-time applications (autonomous vehicles, smart traffic)
Bridges gap between IoT devices and the cloud
content.visual_suggestion: Layered diagram: IoT → Fog → Cloud

content.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
key_points: Network of physical objects with sensors to collect/exchange data
Disadvantages: security risks, complexity, high cost
Applications: Smart Home, Smart City, Supply Chain, Healthcare
content.visual_suggestion: 4-component cycle diagram with smart home example

slides.section: 3.1 - Overview of Relational Database Management System

content.title: RDBMS Overview
key_points: RDBMS = software to create, maintain, and access relational databases
Relational database = data stored in 2D tables
Data Types: Text, Integer, Date/Time, Currency
Primary Key – uniquely identifies each record
Foreign Key – links tables (primary key in another table)
content.visual_suggestion: Table diagram showing fields and records

content.title: Using SQL in Microsoft Access
key_points: SQL = Structured Query Language for databases
Create Query → Switch to SQL View
Write SQL commands in SQL View
Common commands: CREATE, SELECT, UPDATE, INSERT
Double-click saved query to run later
content.visual_suggestion: Screenshot of Access showing SQL View

content.title: DDL - Data Definition Language
key_points: DDL: Create and restructure database objects
• CREATE TABLE – define new table with columns and data types
• ALTER TABLE – modify existing table (add, drop, change columns)
Common data types: CHAR, TEXT, INTEGER, DATETIME, CURRENCY
REFERENCES keyword creates foreign key relationships
content.visual_suggestion: Command syntax examples for CREATE, ALTER, DROP

content.title: DML - Data Manipulation Language
key_points: Use WHERE clause in UPDATE and DELETE to target specific rows
Without WHERE: all rows are affected!
For DELETE, foreign key constraints may prevent deletion
content.visual_suggestion: Example code snippets showing INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

content.title: SELECT - Data Query Language
key_points: Basic syntax: SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... ORDER BY ...
Join tables: SELECT ... FROM table1, table2 WHERE table1.key = table2.key
content.visual_suggestion: Example SELECT query with output table

content.title: XML - Extensible Markup Language
key_points: XML = store and structure data, not present it
Syntax rules: one root, case-sensitive, proper nesting, quoted attributes
content.visual_suggestion: Example XML document with labeled components

content.title: HTML vs. XML Comparison
key_points: • HTML = predefined tags; XML = custom tags
• HTML = tolerant of errors; XML = strict, no errors
content.visual_suggestion: Comparison table with side-by-side examples

content.title: XML: Pros and Cons
content.visual_suggestion: Two-column table: Pros vs Cons

content.title: Website Publishing
key_points: Website = organized files with root directory
Root has subfolders: pages, images, CSS, scripts
Publishing = upload files to web host's remote server
Domain name = unique website address (e.g., moe.gov.et)
Secure sites show locked padlock in browser
content.visual_suggestion: Website directory structure diagram

content.title: Installing Software
key_points: • Insert installation disc or download from source
• Agree to license, enter serial number
• Use trusted app stores only (Google Play, Apple App Store)
• Check security settings to scan for harmful apps
content.visual_suggestion: Step-by-step installation flowchart

content.title: Uninstalling Software
key_points: Reasons: free up space, improve speed
• System apps may be locked (cannot uninstall)
content.visual_suggestion: Screenshot of Programs and Features window

content.title: Software Troubleshooting
key_points: Troubleshooting = systematic approach to find and fix faults
Frozen/slow application: close, reopen, update, or force quit
Slow computer: scan for malware, free disk space, defrag
Sound not working: check volume, speakers, drivers
Task Manager: Ctrl+Alt+Delete to force quit
Consult online resources or experts for persistent issues
content.visual_suggestion: Task Manager screenshot showing frozen app

content.title: System Maintenance Tools
key_points: Disk Defragmenter: rearranges files to improve retrieval
Windows Update: installs security patches and features
Check Disk: scans and fixes hard drive errors
System Restore: creates restore points or reverts to previous state
Close Unwanted Programs: free up memory via Task Manager
content.visual_suggestion: Icons for each system tool with brief description

content.title: Network Troubleshooting Steps & Tools
key_points: Network problems: cable fault, connectivity, config issues
Command-line tools: ipconfig, ping, tracert, nslookup, netstat
content.visual_suggestion: 7-step troubleshooting flowchart

content.title: Network Hardware Maintenance Tools
key_points: Wire Crimper – attaches connectors to cable ends
Punch Down Tool – connects wires to patch panel
Tone Generator – sends signal through wires
content.visual_suggestion: Photos of each hardware tool with labels

content.title: Conditional (Branching) Statements
key_points: Conditionals = program makes decisions at runtime
• if – executes code if condition is true
• if...else – executes one block if true, another if false
Syntax rules: colon (:) after expression, proper indentation
content.visual_suggestion: Flowchart showing if-elif-else decision paths

slides.section: 6.1.2 - Loops or Iteration Program Flow Controls

content.title: Loops (Iteration) in Python
key_points: Loops = repeat a block of code multiple times
For Loop: iterates over a sequence (list, string, range)
While Loop: continues while condition is true
content.visual_suggestion: Code examples showing for and while loops

content.title: Comments in Python
key_points: Comments = descriptive text ignored by interpreter
Purposes: describe code, improve readability, prevent execution
IDLE: Format menu → Comment Out Region (Alt+3)
content.visual_suggestion: Code snippet showing commented and uncommented regions

content.title: Python Interpreter
key_points: Interpreter executes source code line by line
Bytecode executed by Python Virtual Machine (PVM)
IDLE features: interactive mode (REPL) and script execution
content.visual_suggestion: Diagram: Source Code → Bytecode → PVM

content.title: Debugging in Python
key_points: Debugging = process of finding and fixing bugs
Debug Mode: Debug → Debugger in IDLE menu
Set breakpoint: right-click line → Set Breakpoint
Inspect variables in Debug Control Window
content.visual_suggestion: IDLE Debug Control window screenshot
